parameters.description_note: This product renders the religion categories of the 2023 Census of Pakistan exactly as the Pakistan Bureau of Statistics (PBS) prints them in Table 9. The published 2023 categories are Muslim, Christian, Hindu Jati, Qadiani/Ahmadi, Scheduled Castes, Sikh, Parsi, and Others. Qadiani/Ahmadi is the state's enumeration label for the Ahmadiyya community, applied after the 1974 constitutional amendment that declared Ahmadis non-Muslim; the label is carried verbatim as the official record, and is not the project's description of any community's self-understanding. Hindu Jati and Scheduled Castes are enumerated as separate categories in the printed table, and this product combines nothing: each published category is reported as printed. The 2017 census used a different, six-category frame (Muslim, Christian, Hindu, Qadiani/Ahmadi, Scheduled Castes, Others); the frames differ across waves and are not category-comparable, and no cross-wave comparison is made.
parameters.territorial_scope: The 2023 PBS Table 9 religion tables cover the four provinces (Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Punjab, Sindh, and Balochistan) and the Islamabad Capital Territory. They exclude Azad Jammu and Kashmir and Gilgit-Baltistan, whose figures are published separately and are not included here. This product renders the coverage of the published tables as printed and makes no territorial claim.
parameters.sensitivity: Religion is highly sensitive in Pakistan for the Ahmadiyya, Hindu, Christian, Sikh, and Dalit (Scheduled Castes) communities. This is a district-level product (a coarser frame than the tehsil tables the PBS also publishes), chosen to reduce very small cells while rendering the official record. District counts are printed exactly with no PBS suppression rule, and this product applies no small-cell treatment: every published category count is rendered as printed.
parameters.small_cell_treatment: none; district exact counts rendered as published (no PBS suppression rule)
parameters.wave_coverage: ONE wave ships (2023). The 2017 wave is deferred: no 2017 district table is cached (province/division only). See deferred_sources.
parameters.manifest_naming_note: Named to the shipped span (pk-census-religion-2023.json) per the shipped-wave rule; the pk-census-religion family manifest widens to 2017-2023 only when a 2017 district wave is actually built.
parameters.local_cache_hint: Raw PBS Table 9 PDFs and boundary metadata are cached under data/raw/pk_census/ and remain git-ignored.

deferred_sources.source: PBS 2017 census Table 9, district-level provincial tables (Punjab, Sindh, Balochistan, ICT full district files)
deferred_sources.reason: A 2017 district-level product cannot be built from the cache. The cached 2017 files reach only province/division level: table09n_2017_national.pdf carries province rows (PAKISTAN, KP, Punjab, Sindh, Balochistan, FATA); table09_2017_kp.pdf reaches only KP's six divisions; table09_2017_fata.pdf reaches only FATA and DIVISION-1. The full 2017 district/tehsil provincial files were not cached. Downloading them from PBS is the unblock for the second wave; the 2017 frame is a separate six-category per-vintage frame (FATA a separate pre-merger unit) and would ship on its own district frame with no cross-vintage concordance and change withheld across the 2018 FATA-into-KP merger.
National anchor only; subnational 1998 religion is a printed District Census Report route not recovered online in the probe.

No district geometry ships with this product; the boundary lane is HELD as a documented blocker. The geoBoundaries PAK ADM3 (tehsil, boundary ID PAK-ADM3-9618217, represented year 2017, 554 units) layer carries an explicit ODbL licence but is vintage-misaligned to the 2023 district roster, which post-dates it; no evidenced ADM3-to-2023-district mapping is available in this build. The geoBoundaries PAK ADM2 (district, boundary ID PAK-ADM2-60131773, represented year 2019, 126 units) layer's licence is unresolved (the release asserts public domain but carries no explicit licence string) and under-counts the census district frame; it is not used. Consequently land_area_sq_km and all place-density fields are null, and an official or licensed 2023 district boundary layer is the open item before a map can render.

The geoBoundaries PAK ADM3 (tehsil, boundary ID PAK-ADM3-9618217, represented year 2017, 554 units) layer carries an explicit ODbL licence but is vintage-misaligned to the 2023 district roster, which post-dates it; no evidenced ADM3-to-2023-district mapping is available in this build. Minority-share two-slot design (docs/development/minority-share-metric.md, ratified 2026-07-11). The reference group is Muslim, Pakistan's largest published religion category nationally in 2023 (national share 96.3522%). It is declared once and held constant across every area. religious_affiliation_percent := the Muslim share; no_religion_percent := the minority share, the exact complement (every published category outside the reference group summed). This is arithmetic on the published official categories and is not a measure of no religion, belief, practice, or secularity.

tests: Source integrity: every 2023 input matches its route-probe sha256.
Every district row's eight category counts sum to its printed total (all 136 units).
Each province's district totals sum exactly to the published provincial anchor (KP incl. the Malakand Protected Area; Punjab; Sindh; Balochistan; ICT).
The national religion-table total equals its eight-category sum.
The two metric slots are exact complements in every row (percent to 100; count to total).
Computed national shares cross-check the published secondary shares within 0.05pp.
The description note is present in the shipped product and this manifest.

source_datasets.notes: Built by scripts/build_pk_boundary.R into apps/regions/pk/data/pk_district_2022.geojson (136 features (135 joined; Lehri unjoined no-data); sha256 e46c94c9bd3234e795fdab4621ce13b861597c3d4f77dc22e6c4d1b5ad0d6bfe; 2,638,486 bytes at 50 percent mapshaper keep, web weight under 3 MB). Scope: the COD ADM2 layer carries 160 units; the 24 Azad Jammu & Kashmir (10) and Gilgit-Baltistan (14) units are out of the census Table 9 frame and dropped, and the abolished Lehri district (PK218, dissolved back into Sibi and Kachhi in 2018 but retained in COD v01) is carried as a disclosed UNJOINED no-data feature because no evidenced partition of its territory between the two census districts exists, leaving 135 joined district polygons plus the Lehri feature. Crosswalk from COD adm2_name to census area_codes is pinned; every non-identity mapping: Chitral Lower->kp-lower-chitral, Chitral Upper->kp-upper-chitral, D. I. Khan->kp-dera-ismail-khan, Kohistan Lower->kp-lower-kohistan, Kohistan Upper->kp-upper-kohistan, Tor Ghar->kp-torghar, Malakand->kp-malakand (census area_name 'Malakand Protected Area'; same footprint), Leiah->pb-layyah, Central Karachi->sd-karachi-central, East Karachi->sd-karachi-east, South Karachi->sd-karachi-south, Korangi Karachi->sd-korangi, Malir Karachi->sd-malir, Shaheed Benazir Abad->sd-shaheed-benazirabad, Shaheed Sikandarabad->bl-surab; all other in-scope units map by identity slug. KEAMARI TREATMENT: the census publishes Karachi West and Keamari as separate districts, but the licensed COD v01 vintage pre-dates the 21 August 2020 split that carved Keamari out of Karachi West, so the single COD West Karachi polygon (PK729) ships as ONE combined display feature carrying area_code 'sd-karachi-west-keamari-combined' and a documented-combine declaration in its geojson properties (KI KPC/KUC precedent); no geometry is invented or split. Consequently 134 census area_codes map one-to-one to a feature and sd-karachi-west + sd-keamari are jointly represented by the one combined feature. The area_summary census rows are UNCHANGED. For a page to render the combined polygon, a companion runtime-joinable summary row keyed on 'sd-karachi-west-keamari-combined' (summing the sd-karachi-west and sd-keamari counts) must be emitted as a derived view, not a modification of the two published census rows; this derived row was PI-ratified and shipped (see top-level notes).

notes: Derived district area summaries plus the licensed district boundary (pk_district_2022.geojson, COD-AB ADM2 CC BY 3.0 IGO). PI RULING 2026-07-11 (second sitting): treatment ratified — use the official record and report the contest; page copy must state, neutrally and with sources, that the 2023 counts are contested by affected communities while the data render the PBS record verbatim. Keamari display combine PI-RATIFIED: the two published census rows stay verbatim and a derived combined row (sd-karachi-west-keamari-combined) sums them for the fused 2022-vintage polygon, disclosure riding the row flag and the boundary feature. Page lane is the remaining step. Iran/Israel-Palestine render-the-record precedent.
